title: Look Twice
summary: Takemura teaches V to look twice in a Japantown square: a staged scene changes while V sits with their back turned, then comes a quiz.
description: Takemura has decided that V looks once where a trained guard looks twice. He asks V to meet him at a bench in a Japantown square at dusk for a lesson in watching.

start.bringUp: Takemura has watched you cross rooms and decided that you look once. A trained guard looks twice, and he means to teach it without a lecture. He asks you to meet him at a bench in a Japantown square at dusk and says he will explain the exercise there. He brings it up as a rule he has already decided on.

bench.name: the bench about twenty metres from the square

T2.open.01.text: Sit. We begin with sitting. You look at one thing. That is a flaw.

T2.open.02.text: Five people will cross this square. Remember them. Then you will turn around.

T2.open.03.text: Four questions. I will not tell you which.

T2.open.04.text: What did you notice first when you arrived? Be precise.

T2.bark.turn.a.text: Do not turn. Turn only when I say.

T2.bark.watcher.a.text: That one. The one who did not wave.

T2.bark.watcher.b.text: Go. Speak to him. I will cover.

T2.close.01.text: Four of four. I am almost pleased.

T2.close.02.text: Adequate. Return when you can look twice.

g1.asks: What did you notice first when you arrived? Be precise.
g1.know: You are at the square with Takemura and you know the five people who will cross it, each with a trait he has already noted.
g1.secret: He noticed your weapon, your pace and the lookout within the first two seconds, and he has not told you yet.

g2.know: You know which of the extras was the lookout, and you know the answers you have given so far.
g2.secret: Nothing. He wants the truth from you.
g2.wants: You to commit to an answer.

stages.label: Takemura explains the look-twice exercise on a bench
stages.objective: Meet Takemura on the bench by the Japantown square
stages.know: You are meeting Takemura at a bench in a Japantown square at dusk. He will explain the exercise in four sentences and then test you on it.
stages.wants: V to come to the square and sit down to learn.

stages.label: V watches a staged scene in the square for six minutes
stages.objective: Watch the people in the Japantown square with Takemura
stages.know: You stand with Takemura at the edge of the square. Five people cross it: a woman in a red coat who sits on a step, a man with a case who crosses three times, two boys kicking a can, a van that parks and leaves, and an old man at a food stall. One of them is a lookout.
stages.wants: V to watch closely and walk the square if they like.

do.who: a man in a grey jacket at the edge of the square

stages.label: V sits on a bench with the square behind them
stages.objective: Sit on the bench with Takemura, your back to the square
stages.know: You are on a bench about twenty metres from the square with your back to it. While you sit, the scene changes in three small ways: the woman has moved, the van is a different one, and the man no longer carries his case.
stages.wants: V to sit with their back to the square and wait.

stages.label: Takemura asks V who was watching them
stages.objective: Answer Takemura's questions about the square
stages.know: The scene is over and you are on the bench with Takemura. He will ask four questions and this is the first: who was watching you? You know which extra was the lookout.
stages.wants: V to commit to an answer.

stages.label: Takemura points out the lookout and lets V go and speak to him
stages.objective: Go and speak to the lookout Takemura pointed out in the square
stages.know: You picked the lookout, the man who did not wave. Takemura points at him without speaking and lets you go and speak to him. He will cover you.
stages.wants: V to go and speak to the lookout.

do.who: a man in a grey jacket at the edge of the square

sharp.memory: Takemura taught you to look twice in a Japantown square, and you caught the man who was watching you.
sharp.history: Takemura sometimes says look twice at the end of a goodbye.

adequate.memory: You got part of Takemura's exercise right in a Japantown square, and he told you to return when you can look twice.

blind.memory: You could not say who had been watching you, and Takemura called it a beginning.

walked.memory: You left Takemura's lesson before the exercise was over.
